assumptions: A block whose end is not visible is abstained on, except in a new file (--- /dev/null), where the last visible line is end-of-file and closes the block.

Helper resolution reads the diff's visible lines unioned with the file's own text under the working directory ('.', the repoRoot convention guardian's CLI already uses); a helper only counts when its body closes inside the text it was read from.

A helper is a same-file `function name(`, `const|let|var name = (…) =>` / `function`, or Python `def name(` whose closed body matches the framework's assertion pattern. Helpers calling other helpers are not followed.
One weak-test finding is emitted per weak test block (previously at most one per file), so each row names its test; added_ranges is the test's line span.
The existing pytest true-positive fixture gained a dedented context line: without it the block's end was never visible and the new rule abstains, which is the intended behaviour.
